messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — runtime OOM spike detected in serving pool us-west-2-gpu-pool at 2007654321. Affected cluster: redwood-infer-prod-2. Autoscaler bumped but errors persist. Paging sara (oncall) and infra team.

sara (oncall): I'm on it. seeing a surge of OOMs in the metrics dashboard. clients with long-context sessions affected. initiating handoff checklist.

mike: looking at logs now. quick summary: multiple nodes hit OOM within a 4min window, followed by eviction/restart loop.

chen: can you paste the node-level memory stats? suspect KV cache page evictions are causing fragmentation and then a mem cliff.

mike: copying snippets from the leader node (prod-2a-01):
```
[2026-03-15T01:05:12Z] gpu0 total=40GiB used=38.9GiB alloc=36.2GiB free=1.1GiB pageswap=120
[2026-03-15T01:06:05Z] gpu0 free drops to 200MiB, oom kill triggered in runtime (allocation 3.2GiB)
[2026-03-15T01:06:07Z] process redwood-runtime[pid:5421] restarted
```

lucy: interesting — batch sizes were recently increased in A/B experiment for lower p99 latency. maybe the larger batches push memory peaks.

chen: agreed. also seeing KV cache fragment map shows many small allocations; TTL pressure plus batching seems to cause page thrash. hypothesis: increased batch + prefix caching = transient fragmentation -> allocator can't satisfy a contiguous 3GiB request -> OOM.

sara (oncall): customer impact: dashboard shows 12 requests failed in last 10 minutes, mostly gen chat paths with sequence len > 8k. Not yet a broad customer outage but dangerous. Posting note to status page: "Degraded — some generation requests may fail with OOM".

infra-bot: runbook suggestion: 1) lower max_batch_size on affected model routes, 2) enable aggressive KV compaction (experimental), 3) route heavy-context traffic to smaller sequence-slab model.

mike: rolling a quick config change to reduce max_batch_size from 48 -> 24 for the high-memory model (model: redwood-large-v1). applying to prod-2 pool now.

sara (oncall): please confirm the exact command you'll use and whether it needs service restart.

mike: using the runtime feature flag toggle; it updates routing config without full restart. command: 
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  https://controlplane/api/v1/pools/prod-2/config \
  -d '{"routes":{"redwood-large-v1":{"max_batch_size":24}}}'
```
No restart expected. will monitor.

(2m) mike: applied. watching memory.

(4m) mike: immediate reduction in per-request peak on node metrics. free memory rose from ~200MiB to ~1.4GiB on gpu0. no new OOMs reported in last 2m.

chen: can we grab fragmentation stats from jemalloc shim and KV cache free list? snippets:
```
jemalloc_stats: active=35.9GiB mapped=38.5GiB fragmentation=6.8%
kv_cache_fragment: total_alloc=18GiB live=17.2GiB shards=16384 avg_free_chunk=24KiB small_chunks=78%
```

lucy: high small_chunks ratio — explains fragmentation. compaction could help but is risky mid-incident. prefer conservative changes first.

sara (oncall): agree. keep compaction on the table but don't enable unless we see reoccurrence. next step: run a targeted rollback of the A/B experiment that raised batch size for traffic tagged "experiment/high-p99". @mike can you flip the experiment flag?

mike: flipping experiment flag now.

(1m) mike: flag flipped. traffic for that experiment down to baseline. monitoring error rate.

(6m) mike: error rate trending down to normal. CPU/GPU utilization still elevated but stable.

chen: let's collect a timeline and artifacts for the RCA thread:
- event 01:05:12Z — first spike in page swap counts on prod-2a-01
- event 01:06:05Z — contiguous allocation fail -> OOM -> runtime restart
- event 01:06:07Z — node back online, requests retried, tails still saw failures
- event 01:08:00Z — operator reduced max_batch_size (48->24)
- event 01:09:00Z — experiment flag rollback
- event 01:12:00Z — error rate returns to baseline

mike: saving logs to shared S3: s3://redwood-incident-archives/2007654321/logs.tar.gz and perf traces at s3://redwood-incident-archives/2007654321/traces/

lucy: for RCA we'll want: jemalloc dumps, KV cache free list per-shard, runtime allocation traces for the 30s before OOM, and a copy of the A/B config change.

sara (oncall): customer comms: engineering recommends "mitigated, monitoring" for now. I'll draft a short status update and set severity to P2 for postmortem.

infra-bot: reminder: attach incident bot summary and add who was paged, playbook steps taken, and links to artifacts.

mike: note — there are two nodes that still show elevated swap counts (prod-2a-03 and prod-2b-02). I'll schedule a rolling restart during low traffic window and keep you posted.

chen: follow-up hypotheses for RCA:
1) config change increasing batch size raised transient peak allocations beyond allocator contiguous limits.
2) KV cache fragmentation exacerbated by short-lived prefix entries and small chunk churn.
3) jemalloc background coalesce not aggressive enough under steady fragmentation -> periodic mem cliff.

lucy: experiments to run after stabilization: stress test with increased batch but with pre-compact step; run KV compaction in staging with same traffic pattern; evaluate using a different allocator setting (background reclaim tunables).

sara (oncall): thanks team. I'll keep the thread open for RCA notes. tagging @chen @mike @lucy for follow-ups. updating the incident board.

mike: uploading the config diff to the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7891?file=config-diff

(25m) sara (oncall): closing active page. mitigation successful for now. creating a post-incident action list: 1) revert batching experiment fully unless QA signs off; 2) build KV cache compaction feature toggle; 3) add an allocator fragmentation metric and alert (contiguous-free < 4GiB); 4) run chaos test in staging that simulates many short-lived prefixes.

pagerbot: incident closed by sara (oncall) at 2007654390.

sara (oncall): final note — no customer escalations so far. we'll draft RCA doc and circulate to eng-runtime and SRE next 24h.
